Why JDOOM?

Four problems that every network engineer faces -- solved in one browser.

🔗

Too Many Protocol Clients

SSH→PuTTY, Telnet→SecureCRT, RDP→Remote Desktop, SQL→SSMS — a different tool for every port.

▩

Dark Command-Line Terminals

Telnet/SSH shows IAC garbage, non-printable chars are unreadable — dark terminals are useless for real work.

🔎

Port Probing Requires nmap

Need to open a terminal and type commands to identify services — why not just type the address in a browser?

📦

Extensions Can't Install Offline

Air-gapped/isolated networks can’t reach Chrome Web Store — extensions must ship with the browser.

A complete browser first — standard web renders natively

https://jiwo.org

The real production site https://jiwo.org rendered natively in-kernel: tables, colors, images and CJK typography all correct; full HTML5/CSS3/JavaScript support. Only on top of this baseline does the three-stage probe below handle non-web ports.

Three-Stage Probe, light-to-heavy, stop on first match

Three progressive checks on every target port -- each stage can independently return a verdict; never oversteps.

STAGE 1

Read Active Banners

SSH/FTP/SMTP/Telnet self-identify on connect. JDOOM reads the banner and stops — zero interference.

passive
STAGE 2

Try HTTP

Web pages render normally; non-HTTP responses terminate early — no side effects.

standard
STAGE 3

Service Fingerprinting

Minimal handshake packets identify RDP/SQL/SMB/RPC/SSL — only for non-web ports.

active
